ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of using a voucher (share of patients)
ground_truth.location: Table 3, column (1) Used Voucher, beta_P: Patient Voucher
ground_truth.context: Table 3 ("Impacts on Malaria Treatment Outcomes"), column (1). Linear probability model of an indicator that the patient redeemed a voucher for a free course of ACT tablets (simple malaria treatment), from the administrative voucher records, on dummies for Patient Voucher days (vouchers handed to patients on arrival, before the consultation) and Doctor Voucher days (vouchers given to the health workers to assign at their discretion), relative to Control days, with clinic visit date fixed effects and additional controls chosen by post-double-selection lasso (Belloni, Chernozhukov and Hansen 2014) from clinic dummies, symptom dummies, illness duration (top-coded at the 99th percentile) and its square, patient age and its square, an under-five dummy, patient gender, pregnancy, whether the patient answered the survey, respondent gender, Bambara ethnicity, French speaking, literacy, primary education or less, a home follow-up survey dummy, and all pairwise interactions of the patient and respondent controls; missing values recoded to the sample mean and dummied out.  Sample: acutely ill patients interviewed at the study clinics in Bamako, Mali.  The entry is the Patient Voucher coefficient.  Standard errors clustered by clinic.

i4r.notes: Blanket I4R verdict (team 23); the row adds back non-malaria voucher users, 0.33 (0.029).

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=0.299555 vs claimed=0.35 (relative error 14.41%, tolerance 8.57%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.03).
